proposed_core_edits.reason: The tuning handle must index regularization of the published OVS normal operator used by the target estimator, rather than the obsolete aggregate comparison operator.

The existing definition regularizes \(H\) and \(b^\star\), neither of which enters the proved attaining estimator.  The complete replacement targets \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) and its projection coefficient, states the data and tuning inputs, and records the local-class and nonvacuity requirements without asserting a uniform theorem.

proposed.justification: Rank changes in the published conditional normal operator are the nonregular boundary relevant to the attaining estimator; they cannot be hidden inside a fixed-rank pointwise theorem, and coverage must be paired with a length or power criterion to be nonvacuous.
proposed.gap: The established finite-support result treats only fixed laws with separated positive rank.  Neither the staggered DiD and DDD literature nor this note supplies uniform inference over declared local sequences with weak or changing eigenvalues of the published normal operator under explicit nuisance envelopes and a nonvacuity criterion.
proposed.consumer: A solution would stabilize the optional efficient target-inference backend when published OVS normal directions are nearly redundant.  Comparator-KKT rank adaptation would remain a separate extension for efficiency-gap inference.

obligation.what_is_open: A nonvacuous uniformly valid confidence procedure has not been characterized over an explicitly specified local-sequence class in which positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P_n}(X)\) may approach zero or its rank may change on covariate sets of positive probability.
obligation.obstruction: The map \((K,r)\mapsto K^\dagger r\) has no uniform perturbation modulus near a rank change without quantitative compatibility: in a vanishing-eigenvalue direction \(v\), the coefficient is \(v'r/\lambda\), whereas the exact-law range condition at \(\lambda=0\) alone supplies no local bound on this ratio.  The fixed-support estimates have only pointwise error control, and coverage alone admits the vacuous interval \(\mathbb R\).  Thus a local eigenvalue/nuisance envelope and an expected-length, diameter, or power criterion are mathematically necessary to pose either a positive construction or an impossibility theorem.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-rank argument was transferred from the obsolete aggregate operator to the actual published system.  Proposition \(\mathrm{\ref{prop:ovs-normal-finite-support-rates}}\) controls \(\widehat K_{\mathrm{OVS}}-K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and \(\widehat r_{\mathrm{OVS}}-r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) at root-\(n\) rate and recovers rank at each separated fixed law.  Extending the Moore--Penrose perturbation calculation to local eigenvalues introduces reciprocal powers of the smallest retained eigenvalue, so the available remainder is not uniform without declared eigenvalue and nuisance envelopes.  No comparator-KKT calculation is relevant to target-estimator adaptation.

prose_updates.tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, the exhaustive period-admissible normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) yields the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) and bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\); the clean-through-terminal local model and the aggregate pairwise-score family form two larger frontiers.  A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains the published bound.  Aggregate, localized, and published equality are diagnosed separately.  A bounded binary family makes all three normal closures coincide and gives the exact published-bound gain \(3/512\).  Away from equality and rank changes, an explicit finite-moment plug-in gives pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound efficiency gap.  Uniform rank-adaptive target inference remains an explicitly scoped question for the published operator \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\), requiring a local-sequence envelope and a nonvacuous length or power criterion; comparator-KKT rank changes are a separate gap-inference extension.

project_justification.niche: The published OVS model has more period-specific normal directions than either terminal clean-comparison contrasts or the localized clean-through-terminal model.  Singular published-normal systems, shared outcome cells, and law-dependent comparator weights must be treated coherently.  For target inference the relevant nonregular boundary is the rank of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\); ranks of comparator KKT systems concern only the separate efficiency-gap problem.

prose_updates.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise benchmark.  This note adds the exhaustive published OVS normal, its attaining fixed-support correction, and pointwise inference for the law-dependent comparator's published-bound gap.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie give related conditional efficiency results for staggered DiD, but not the eligibility-gap tangent system.  Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; the affine quotient, absolute-eigenvalue selected-rank derivative, and DDD moment reconstruction are proved here.  Generic DML theory supplies the cross-fitting template but not the all-cohort shared-cell calculation.  Uniform adaptation to weak or changing eigenvalues of the published normal operator is not supplied by these references or claimed here; it remains open until a local experiment, nuisance envelope, and length or power criterion are fixed.  Comparator-KKT rank adaptation is distinct and pertains to gap inference.
prose_updates.interpretation: There are three precision frontiers.  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family.  Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound.  Projection against the exhaustive \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the smaller published bound.  A comparator reaches these frontiers when, respectively, \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0\), \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\), and \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\).  The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend can report all three diagnostics and can expose gap Wald inference in the certified fixed-support branch.  Its target-estimation rank-adaptation question concerns the learned published projection \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), not \(H\) or \(b^\star\); comparator-KKT rank changes belong to a separate gap-inference extension.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law and permits singular or redundant normal coordinates.  Target attainment and gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support.  The gap theorem assumes positive influence variance and is separated from equality by \(\delta_0>0\); it is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes.  The published-normal finite-sieve characterization does not establish a growing-sieve remainder for continuous covariates.  No uniform target confidence procedure is proved when positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) approach zero or its rank changes: such a theorem requires an explicit local law class, eigenvalue and nuisance-rate envelopes relative to the regularization scale, and a nonvacuity criterion based on interval length or power.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at interior laws admitting a full-data extension in the global OVS model.  It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\).  Cross-fitted target inference and plug-in efficiency-gap inference are pointwise fixed-support results.  The \(3/512\) witness is genuinely relative to the published bound because all three normal closures coincide.  No continuous-covariate gap Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.  The open rank-adaptive target problem is confined to \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) and requires a specified local sequence and length or power standard; comparator-KKT rank changes form a separate, unresolved gap-inference extension.
